  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Reviewing Incident Reports}

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "#>")
library(eatPrep)

# Exercise the review without interactive input when building the vignette.
review_example <- function(dat, info, useGroups = attr(info, "reviewGroup"),
                           nonValidValues = c(-99, -98, -97, -96),
                           choice = "yes, all values") {
  group <- if (is.null(useGroups)) attr(info, "ID") else useGroups
  answers <- c(rep(choice, length(unique(info[[group]]))), "yes")
  review <- visualSubsetRecode
  env <- new.env(parent = environment(review))
  env$.subset_menu <- function(choices) {
    stopifnot(length(answers) > 0L, answers[1] %in% choices)
    answer <- answers[1]
    answers <<- answers[-1]
    answer
  }
  environment(review) <- env
  invisible(capture.output(result <- suppressMessages(review(
    dat, info, useGroups = useGroups, nonValidValues = nonValidValues,
    toRecodeVal = "mci"))))
  stopifnot(length(answers) == 0L, result$status == "completed")
  result
}
```

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [checkSubsetIncidents()](../reference/checkSubsetIncidents.html) | Check IDs, affected responses and design assignments. |
| [prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html) | Select the reported person-response pairs. |
| [visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html) | Review and recode by class or person; pause and resume. |

## 1. Inputs

Use your response data, a **long incident table**, and the design tables from
**one input list**. No separate class roster is needed. Keep existing ID column
names and choose the response level explicitly:

```{r settings}
library(eatPrep)
student_id <- "learner_key"
class_id <- "group_key"
data_level <- "unit"  # Use "subunit" for original or recoded subunit columns.
```

The student-ID column must occur in `dat`, `incidents` and `inputList$rotation`;
the class-ID column in `dat` and `incidents`. Student IDs must be unique, and
class IDs must identify classes across schools.

<details>
<summary>Runnable example inputs (all identifiers and values are fictional)</summary>

```{r example-inputs}
dat <- data.frame(
  learner_key = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  group_key = c("K1", "K1", "K1", "K2", "K2"),
  U12 = c("mbi", "1", "2", "1", NA), U3 = c("1", "mnr", "0", "1", "1")
)
inputList <- list(
  subunits = data.frame(
    subunit = c("I1", "I2", "I3"), subunitRecoded = c("I1R", "I2R", "I3R"),
    unit = c("U12", "U12", "U3")
  ),
  blocks = data.frame(
    subunit = c("I1", "I2", "I3"), block = c("b1", "b1", "b2"),
    subunitBlockPosition = c(1, 2, 1)
  ),
  booklets = data.frame(
    booklet = c("X", "Y"), block1 = c("b1", "b2"), block2 = c("b2", "b1")
  ),
  rotation = data.frame(learner_key = dat$learner_key,
                        booklet = c("X", "Y", "X", "X", "Y"))
)
incidents <- data.frame(
  group_key = c("K1", "K1", "K1", "K2"),
  learner_key = c("A", "A", "B", NA), blockPosition = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  comment = c("Display error", "Display error", "Interrupted test", "Audio failure")
)
```

</details>

Each incident row names **one affected block position**. Keep repeated persons
on separate rows. Positions refer to each person's booklet: in this example,
position 1 means block b1 for A, but b2 for B.

| Person IDs within a class's incident rows | Selection |
|---|---|
| All supplied | Exactly the reported person-position pairs. |
| All missing (`NA`, empty or whitespace) | All members of that class in `dat`, at the reported positions. |
| Mixed supplied and missing | Error: clarify the intended selection. |

The example selects A at positions 1 and 2, B at position 1, and everyone in K2
at position 2. C is not selected. Optional `issueId` and `level` columns usually
need not be supplied; `comment` is optional too.

## 2. Check

```{r preflight}
checked <- checkSubsetIncidents(
  dat, incidents, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  subunits = inputList$subunits, dataLevel = data_level,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)
checked
```

Use **distinct counts**, rather than counting repeated problem records:

```{r inspect-check, eval=FALSE}
checked$summary[c("missingPersons", "missingClasses", "missingUnits", "readyRows")]
checked$missing  # Identifiers behind the missing counts.
print(checked, max_problems = 10)
unique(checked$ignored[c("subunit", "unit", "ignoredReason")])
```

`$problems` contains findings to inspect; `$ignored` lists omitted design entries
without usable response columns. Preparation skips absent persons/classes by
default (`unmatched = "drop"`) and retains the report. Contradictory assignments,
ambiguities affecting existing responses and unresolved reported positions still
stop preparation, as does an entirely empty selection. Use `unmatched = "error"`
for strict handling of absent cases.

The review covers the **available data and reported incidents**. Broader metadata
checks remain separate: [checkInputList()](../reference/checkInputList.html) and
[checkDesign()](../reference/checkDesign.html). Missing-item totals are provisional
when `checked$summary$itemCheckComplete` is `FALSE`.

## 3. Prepare and review

Use the same ID names, response level and input list for preparation:

```{r selection}
info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  dat, incidents = incidents, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  subunits = inputList$subunits, dataLevel = data_level,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)
```

In unit mode, **any affected subunit selects its entire unit**. Here I1 and I2
both select U12, which is displayed and recoded once per person. Supply the
complete `inputList$subunits` table; subunit names and unit response names may differ.

```{r class-review, eval=FALSE}
result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci", nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"),
  positions = TRUE, comments = TRUE
)
```

This gives **one decision per class**. Different item/position layouts appear in
separate tables within that decision. `positions = TRUE` adds the two rows below
the responses and enables block selection; `comments = TRUE` shows incident
comments. Both switches accept `TRUE` or `FALSE`. For the first class:

```{r response-display, echo=FALSE}
eatPrep:::.subset_display(dat, info[info[[class_id]] == "K1", ], student_id, TRUE)
```

Multiple within-block positions are comma-separated. Semicolons separate paired
block groups when a unit spans several blocks; selecting any reported block
position selects the whole unit. The full mapping remains in `info`.

Choose **all values**, **all non-valid values**, or **specific blocks** in the
menu. `nonValidValues` controls only the second choice: supply numeric codes or
text codes as in the example. Its default is `c(-99, -98, -97, -96)`; matching
uses original responses, even after revisiting a group. `NA` responses stay missing.
**Reset** withdraws the group's previous recoding; **no** leaves it unchanged.

## 4. Individual review and resuming

For one decision per person, pass `useGroups = NULL` explicitly:

```{r individual-review, eval=FALSE}
result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, useGroups = NULL, nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"), toRecodeVal = "mci"
)
```

All incident rows for a person are combined. For data without classes, use
`classID = NULL` in both checking and preparation; every incident must then name
a person, and class-level reports are not allowed.

For longer reviews, choose a new checkpoint file and use the pause menu:

```{r checkpoint, eval=FALSE}
result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"),
  toRecodeVal = "mci", checkpoint = "review.rds"
)
# After pausing, including in a later R session:
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds")
```

Resume with `state` alone: it retains the original data, decisions and settings,
including `nonValidValues`. Continue processing with `result$dat`; inspect decisions
in `result$subsetInfo`. For the legacy `issues` format and all argument details,
see [prepareSubsetInfo()](../reference/prepareSubsetInfo.html) and
[visualSubsetRecode()](../reference/visualSubsetRecode.html).

```{r verify-results, include=FALSE}
by_class <- review_example(dat, info)
by_person <- review_example(dat, info, useGroups = NULL)
expected <- dat
expected$U12[1] <- "mci"
expected$U3[c(1, 2, 4)] <- "mci"
filtered <- review_example(dat, info, nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"),
                            choice = "yes, all non-valid values (mbi, mnr)")
expected_filtered <- dat
expected_filtered$U12[1] <- "mci"
expected_filtered$U3[2] <- "mci"
stopifnot(checked$summary$readyRows == 4L,
          identical(by_class$dat, expected), identical(by_person$dat, expected),
          identical(filtered$dat, expected_filtered),
          identical(by_class$state$groups, c("K1", "K2")),
          identical(by_person$state$groups, c("A", "B", "D", "E")))
```
